quests.instruction: Shadow the warm remark. How is 'that' pronounced after 'glad'?
quests.word: I'm really glad that you could make it tonight.
quests.textToSpeak: I'm really glad that you could make it tonight.
options: Dropped completely, so it sounds like 'glad you'
quests.ipa: /aɪm ˈrɪəli ˈɡlæd ðət jə kəd ˈmeɪk ɪt təˈnaɪt/
quests.hint: Compare it with 'Look at that!' where 'that' carries the stress.
quests.explanation: Here 'that' is a conjunction introducing a clause, so it has no stress and reduces to /ðət/; the beats fall on 'glad' and 'make'.
quests.flowRule: Weak Forms: the conjunction 'that' is /ðət/ when it introduces a clause.

quests.instruction: Shadow the answer. Why is the first 'can' strong?
quests.word: Yes, I can, but I'd rather not.
quests.textToSpeak: Yes, I can, but I'd rather not.
options: A short answer ends on it, so it must take its full /kæn/ form
'Can' is always /kæn/ in every sentence and style
It follows 'I', which forces the strong form every time
quests.correctAnswer: A short answer ends on it, so it must take its full /kæn/ form
quests.ipa: /ˈjes | aɪ ˈkæn | bət aɪd ˈrɑːðə ˈnɒt/
quests.hint: Compare it to 'I can come.'
quests.explanation: At the end of a clause, 'can' has no following word to lean on, so it keeps its strong form.
quests.flowRule: Strong Forms: a function word at the end of a clause is not reduced.

quests.instruction: Shadow the question. Why is 'at' strong here?
quests.word: What are you looking at?
quests.textToSpeak: What are you looking at?
options: It is always /æt/ in every kind of sentence
It sits at the end of the clause, after the verb, so it keeps /æt/
The speaker is angry, so every word becomes strong
quests.correctAnswer: It sits at the end of the clause, after the verb, so it keeps /æt/
quests.ipa: /ˈwɒt ə jə ˈlʊkɪŋ ˈæt/
quests.hint: Notice what comes after 'at' compared with the phrase 'look at it'.
quests.explanation: Because nothing follows 'at', it cannot lean on a following word and keeps its full vowel /æt/; this stranded preposition can even carry some stress.
quests.flowRule: Strong Forms: a function word that ends a clause keeps its full vowel.

quests.instruction: Shadow the complaint. What happens to 'for you'?

quests.explanation: 'For' becomes /fə/ before 'you', which takes the stress and emphasises the listener.
quests.flowRule: Weak Forms: 'for' reduces to /fə/ before a stressed word.

quests.explanation: 'Some' is introducing the noun and not contrasting, so it is weak /səm/.
quests.flowRule: Weak Forms: unstressed 'some' is /səm/.

quests.instruction: Shadow the instruction. What happens to 'her' after 'give'?

quests.explanation: Negative 'can't' must remain distinct from 'can', so it keeps a long vowel.
